q: מהו תומך בקבלת החלטות לפי חוק הכשרות המשפטית והאפוטרופסות?
o: אפוטרופוס המקבל החלטות במקום האדם מכוח מינוי שיפוטי ובהתאם לסמכויות שנקבעו
אדם הממונה לסייע בקבלת החלטות מבלי להחליף את שיקול דעתו של האדם
עורך דין שמחליט במקום האדם על הטיפול הרפואי משום שהוא מייצג אותו בהליך המשפטי
עובד סוציאלי שמקבל את ההחלטה הסופית במקום האדם לאחר שהסביר לו את החלופות
explanation:
תומך בקבלת החלטות מנגיש מידע ומסייע בהבנת חלופות ובמימוש הבחירה. הסמכות להחליט נשארת אצל האדם. **אדם הממונה לסייע בקבלת החלטות מבלי להחליף את שיקול דעתו של האדם**.

**א. אפוטרופוס המקבל החלטות במקום האדם מכוח מינוי שיפוטי ובהתאם לסמכויות שנקבעו.** אפוטרופסות עשויה להעביר סמכות בתחום מוגדר.
**ב. אדם הממונה לסייע בקבלת החלטות מבלי להחליף את שיקול דעתו של האדם.** סיוע בלי החלפת שיקול הדעת הוא מטרת התמיכה.
**ג. עורך דין שמחליט במקום האדם על הטיפול הרפואי משום שהוא מייצג אותו בהליך המשפטי.** ייצוג משפטי כשלעצמו אינו מסמיך לבחור טיפול.
**ד. עובד סוציאלי שמקבל את ההחלטה הסופית במקום האדם לאחר שהסביר לו את החלופות.** עובד סוציאלי יכול לסייע ואינו מקבל את ההחלטה במקום האדם.

אסמכתא · חוק הכשרות המשפטית והאפוטרופסות, התשכ״ב–1962, סעיף 67ב, עמ׳ 61–62.

q: A 69-year-old man is found to have new anemia on routine testing. There are currently no findings suggesting a hematologic malignancy, and no etiologic work-up has been performed. Which group of tests belongs in the initial evaluation described by Hazzard?
o: Blood count and reticulocytes, followed by marrow aspiration and biopsy to identify hematologic disease
Blood count and reticulocytes, iron and vitamin studies, and renal, thyroid, and liver tests
Erythropoietin, copper, zinc, and C-reactive protein measurements to investigate additional causes
Serum protein electrophoresis, lactate dehydrogenase, and haptoglobin measurements to investigate additional causes
explanation:
An initial anemia work-up asks whether the marrow is responding and whether a common reversible cause is present. Reticulocytes measure production of new red cells.

**Start with a blood count and differential, reticulocytes, iron and vitamin studies, and renal, thyroid and liver tests.**

**A. Blood count followed by marrow biopsy.** The blood tests belong first. Marrow sampling requires a reason to suspect a marrow disorder.
**B. Broad initial blood tests.** These assess cell lines, red-cell production, iron stores, B12 and folate, and organ dysfunction that can impair erythropoiesis.
**C. Erythropoietin, copper, zinc and CRP.** These are selective second-line tests when the first evaluation or clinical context points in that direction.
**D. Electrophoresis, LDH and haptoglobin.** These target a plasma-cell disorder or hemolysis. They do not replace the common-cause evaluation.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1480.

q: An older man with glaucoma and cognitive impairment has a complex regimen of eye drops and other medications. It is unclear whether he uses them as prescribed. Which principle should guide review?
o: Clarify actual use and simplify to an effective medication regimen
Add medications from the recorded list before asking about actual use
Exclude eye drops from the review and concentrate on oral medications
Increase dosing frequency and regimen complexity to improve adherence
explanation:
A prescribed list may differ from what a patient can manage at home. Eye drops are part of the regimen and require their own administration schedule.

**Clarify actual use, then simplify while preserving treatment benefit.** Cognitive impairment makes it particularly important to ask how the drops and tablets are taken.

**A. Clarify and simplify.** Reviewing each product, route, and timing can uncover omitted doses and identify a schedule the patient can follow.
**B. Add drugs from the recorded list.** Treating an unverified list as actual use risks duplicating treatment or escalating for presumed treatment failure.
**C. Exclude eye drops.** Omitting the glaucoma treatment overlooks the practical difficulty of instilling drops on schedule.
**D. Increase dosing frequency.** More administration times give a patient already struggling more opportunities to miss a dose.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 313.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

q: In which population was durvalumab studied in the PACIFIC trial as described in Hazzard?
o: Resectable stage III NSCLC after complete surgical resection
Stage IV NSCLC after disease control with chemotherapy
Unresectable stage III NSCLC after concurrent chemoradiation
Unresectable stage III NSCLC after sequential chemotherapy and radiation
explanation:
PACIFIC tested durvalumab as consolidation for **unresectable stage III NSCLC controlled after concurrent chemoradiation**. This sequence matters when applying the result.

**A. After complete resection.** Postoperative adjuvant treatment was not the clinical setting.
**B. Controlled stage IV after chemotherapy.** Metastatic disease and chemotherapy alone differ from locally advanced definitive chemoradiation.
**C. Unresectable stage III after concurrent therapy.** These patients had completed concurrent treatment without progression before randomization.
**D. After sequential treatment.** The defining regimen in the trial gave chemotherapy and radiation concurrently.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1426.

. After sequential treatment.** The defining regimen in the trial gave chemotherapy and radiation concurrently.

q: An 80-year-old man with Parkinson disease is found confused and nearly unresponsive. Temperature is 32.5 degrees C, blood pressure 90/55, and heart rate 48. He takes carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 mg four times daily, pramipexole 1 mg three times daily, benztropine 1 mg twice daily, and chlorpromazine 50 mg at bedtime for chronic hiccups. Recent TSH is 4.2 and creatinine 1.8; ECG shows J waves. Rewarming has begun. Which explanation warrants a medication review while rewarming continues?
o: Review chlorpromazine as a reversible contributor
Use the near-normal TSH to rule out a drug effect
Use J waves to identify a primary cardiac cause
Attribute the low temperature to the ambient exposure alone
explanation: Chlorpromazine can impair thermoregulation. Review it as a reversible contributor while rewarming and evaluating other causes. A near-normal TSH does not exclude a medication effect. J waves accompany hypothermia and do not establish a primary cardiac cause. Environmental exposure and drug effects can coexist. Hazzard Ch 39 — SYSTEMS PHYSIOLOGY OF AGING AND SELECTED DISORDERS OF HOMEOSTASIS.
ref: Hazzard Ch 39 — SYSTEMS PHYSIOLOGY OF AGING AND SELECTED DISORDERS OF HOMEOSTASIS

q: בן 88, סובל מפצע לחץ בטרוכנטר ימין. ראה תמונה 2. הוא מטופל בביתו ע"י משפחתו המעוניינים בטיפול האופטימלי עבור ומוכנים לקנות כל תכשיר. מה התכשיר המומלץ לניקוי הפצע לפני החלפת חבישה?
o: מי חמצן 3%
תמיסת NaCl 0.9%
מים מינרלים סטריליים
Polydin 10%
explanation:
Cleansing at dressing changes removes loose debris while protecting viable tissue. The photograph shows a partly red wound bed, and the history gives no clinical signs requiring treatment of invasive infection.

**Gently irrigate with 0.9% sodium chloride.** Isotonic saline is suitable for routine cleansing of viable tissue. Reassess separately if necrosis or infection develops.

**A. Hydrogen peroxide 3%.** Peroxide can injure the fibroblasts involved in repair and should be avoided on open pressure wounds.
**B. Sodium chloride 0.9%.** Gentle irrigation with this physiologic solution removes surface material without exposing the healing bed to an antiseptic.
**C. Sterile mineral water.** Water of suitable quality can also be used for routine wound cleansing. Sterile mineral water offers no specific advantage over the isotonic fluid listed here.
**D. Povidone-iodine 10%.** An antiseptic may have a role in a wound with substantial debris or infection. Routine application to clean, healing tissue can impair fibroblast activity.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 692–693, 697. WHS pressure ulcer guidelines, 2023 update, guideline 4.5.

q: מה מהבאים מעלה את הסיכון לאספירציה אחרי הניתוח?
o: כאב לאחר ניתוח
אטלקטזיס לאחר ניתוח
ניתוח אורטופדי
המצאות בקע סרעפתי
explanation:
Aspiration occurs when material enters the airway. Risk rises if gastric contents reflux into the esophagus or swallowing and airway protection are impaired. **Of these findings, a hiatal hernia favors perioperative aspiration.**

**A. Postoperative pain** Pain can limit deep breaths and coughing. It does not explain the reflux mechanism being tested.
**B. Atelectasis** Collapsed or poorly aerated lung units are a pulmonary complication. Atelectasis does not cause gastric contents to reflux.
**C. Orthopedic surgery** Procedure type affects the overall pulmonary risk. It is less specific for aspiration than an anatomical factor that favors reflux.
**D. Hiatal hernia** A hernia at the hiatus favors gastroesophageal reflux. Reduced lower-esophageal sphincter tone, delayed gastric emptying or impaired swallowing can compound that risk.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, ch. 27, pp. 375–377, especially Other Concerns on p. 376.
